text: I can trace a word-count job through split, map, partition, shuffle, sort and reduce, naming where each step's data lives.
I can estimate shuffle volume with and without a combiner and say which aggregations a combiner can't handle.
I can diagnose a skewed reducer and fix it with a broadcast join or key salting.
I can explain which tasks MapReduce re-runs after a worker failure and why backup tasks fix slow machines but not skew.
I can make a nightly ETL or ELT job idempotent with atomic partition overwrites so retries and backfills are safe.
I can argue both sides of lambda vs kappa for a given retention and reprocessing requirement, with replay-time arithmetic.
